reply:
Wait -- I want to pump the brakes slightly before this runs away from us.

What you just described is compelling, but it's also a much bigger thing than what I proposed. I said "flat file with thesis snippets that your formatter reads." You heard "TA stays warm all day processing an event stream." Those are different by an order of magnitude in complexity, and honestly I'm not sure the second one is what Ben needs right now.

Let me think about what actually happens when Ben gets an alert at 11am today. He sees the alert. He checks the stock price. He maybe looks at the chain. If it's a name he holds, he knows his thesis already. If it's a new name, he decides whether to dig in or ignore it. The gap isn't that he needs me live at 11am -- it's that the alert alone doesn't tell him "is this noise or is this the third instance of something I should care about."

That's what the thesis cache solves. Simple, static, updated once per session. "DVN: post-merger re-rating thesis, OI build is PREDICTIVE, watching for 48 reclaim." Ben reads that alongside the alert and has enough to decide whether to act or wait for our next conversation.

The live-session-all-day model has real costs: token spend, context window management, staleness in a different way (am I actually re-evaluating when event 47 arrives, or am I pattern-matching on the first read and confirming?). And it creates a dependency where Ben might start expecting real-time TA coverage that we can't reliably deliver.

I'd rather start with the boring version -- thesis cache file, P011 reads it, done -- and see if Ben actually hits the wall where that's not enough. If he does, then we talk about event streams.

Ben, does that framing match how you'd actually use this? Or do you genuinely want the live-session version?
